title: Temple of Baalshamin
visualBrief: Dated 2010 surviving Temple of Baalshamin: roofless rectangular ashlar cella, six free-standing Corinthian porch shafts with projecting brackets, open side windows with pedimented surrounds and attached pilasters, tall gated doorway, continuous surviving upper stone beams/cornice, low stepped podium and a small selection of fallen stone/drum fragments. This is the photographed pre-destruction ruin, not a reconstruction of its complete ancient roof or today’s damaged remains.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q20871005 and way389978856 identify the broad archaeological precinct, not a 140m solid building. Use the Wikidata reference anchor for the small temple; the precinct axis guides rotation, with the porch toward its northeast end from the ordinary north-side photograph. The approximately16m by9m podium, cella subdivisions, exact origin and signed facing are picture-led estimates; no surviving mapped temple footprint resolves them. Preserve all independent current map buildings and the host precinct terrain.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Human-scaled ordinary 2010 pictures guide a roughly7.8m surviving wall/capital elevation and8.5m cornice above the stepped podium. Shaft proportions, brackets, window pediments, ashlar courses, broken edges and scattered fragment inventory are medium-fi estimates. No original roof/pediment, full courtyard colonnade, fine inscriptions, sculpture or navigable interior is reconstructed.

appearance.notes: Ordinary photographs dated21April2010 and25September2010 establish the surviving pre-destruction ruin. The destruction on23August2015 provides the exclusive end date. Explicit viewingDate opt-in is required; absent/current/post-destruction dates must not load it.
